firing.source: var sum = 0, i; for(i = 0; i < 10; i++){ if(i <= 5) { continue; } sum += i; }

findings.message: This loop uses `continue`, which jumps to the next iteration from the middle of the body. A reader tracing what happens on one pass has to hold every `continue` above their position in mind, because any of them may have skipped the code they are looking at, and in a `for` loop the update expression still runs while the rest of the body does not. Inverting the condition and wrapping the remainder in an `if` says the same thing with the skip visible in the shape of the code rather than in a jump.

clean.source: var sum = 0, i = 0; while(i < 10) { if(i > 5) { sum += i; } i++; }
